details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1030-1048 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The check_error branch in compare_against_baseline appends a violation without consulting the baseline, so pre-existing unreadable or out-of-tree fingerprint errors are treated as resolver regressions.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers reported the same persistent path error in both baseline and current trees still exits 1 instead of being classified as unchanged drift.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:219-221,284-286 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The _read_file and _path_exists wrappers are dead code and discard the richer error-tuple information from the _result helpers.
  WHY: They are unused today, but keeping wrappers that drop error details can mislead future callers into reintroducing silent-fail behavior.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:178-286 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The helper/result path still ignores the error component in caches and callers, so persistent read/probe failures can be dropped silently.
  WHY: This can make compare-mode treat a baseline-passing error as satisfied or vice-versa and produce incomplete working-set results.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1213-1218 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: A malformed baseline file causes compare mode to fall back to absolute verification instead of failing the baseline path.
  WHY: That changes emitted PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 markers between runs and makes verifier output non-deterministic.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:945-984 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The bootstrap sequence can leave stale branch copies of the support scripts in place when the main snapshot is missing or not used.
  WHY: On a wedged integration branch, the old branch version can still bootstrap and bypass the new resolver/delta-verification fixes.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:509-530,1199-1210 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: capture_baseline_state is invoked without forwarding the resolved ref in baseline-capture mode.
  WHY: The baseline JSON records head_sha for the working tree instead of the intended ref, so compare mode may use the wrong baseline and emit spurious drift markers.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:429-461 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The baseline state file is captured before retries but not preserved or restored across retry attempts.
  WHY: Later retries can compare against stale or re-captured state, defeating the delta-verification contract.
- docs/completed/integration-sync-resolver-self-heal-plan.md:626-629 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The displayed link text and the actual relative target point to different locations for the judge-loop plan reference.
  WHY: Readers following the link can land on a stale or confusing copy instead of the intended active plan.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:972 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: _emit_pre_existing_drift_marker interpolates raw path and pattern values without escaping.
  WHY: Captured regexes with quotes or special characters can confuse downstream drift-audit parsers and break marker deduplication.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:945-984 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: review_conflict_resolve.sh and review_conflict_prepare.sh are installed in both the required and main-primary bootstrap loops, making the source of truth ambiguous.
  WHY: The double install is redundant today and can obscure whether operators are getting the main-snapshot safety fixes.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1043-1047 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When _evaluate_fp_state returns a state with check_error not None, compare mode unconditionally appends the violation and continues without consulting the baseline index.
  WHY: A persistent unreadable or out-of-tree fingerprint path that existed in both baseline and current trees still hard-fails verification instead of being treated as pre-existing unchanged drift.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:219-221 and 284-286 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Both _read_file and _path_exists are thin wrappers that discard the error tuple from _read_file_result / _path_exists_result respectively.
  WHY: They are defined but never called by any function in the codebase, and keeping wrappers that drop error details can mislead future callers into reintroducing silent-fail behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~1046-1048 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: In compare mode, when _evaluate_fp_state returns a check_error, the code immediately appends a violation without checking whether the same error existed in the baseline state.
  WHY: A persistent file-access problem that existed in both baseline and current tree will hard-fail verification even though the resolver did not introduce the problem.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:~1213-1218 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the baseline JSON file is malformed, the verifier prints a warning and falls back to absolute verification instead of staying on the compare path.
  WHY: This makes verifier output non-deterministic and can change the set of PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 markers emitted between runs.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:957-973 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS loop installs scripts from the branch ref first, and MAIN_PRIMARY_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS only overwrites them if a main snapshot exists.
  WHY: If the main snapshot is missing, the stale branch version remains in place and the new delta-verification code is not exercised.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:1199-1210 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: capture_baseline_state() is called without forwarding the resolved ref when baseline capture mode is active.
  WHY: Baseline JSON records the working tree's state under head_sha instead of the intended ref, so compare mode uses the wrong baseline and may emit spurious drift markers.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:509-530 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The baseline capture path forwards ref into the CLI parser but does not pass it through to capture_baseline_state() when that function is called.
  WHY: Verified head_sha in baseline JSON will mismatch the ref being verified in compare mode.
=== END FINDINGS FROM mistralai_mistral-small-2603 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:around lines 1030-1040 in compare_against_baseline() | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When _evaluate_fp_state returns a check_error, compare mode appends a violation without first consulting the baseline to see if the same error existed before.
  WHY: A persistent file-access problem that is unreadable in both baseline and current trees will hard-fail comparison even though the resolver did not introduce the problem.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:lines 945-984 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS loop installs review_conflict_resolve.sh and review_conflict_prepare.sh from the branch checkout first, then MAIN_PRIMARY_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS attempts to overwrite them with the main snapshot.
  WHY: If the main snapshot file is stale or unavailable, the old branch copy can remain active and the self-heal code on main is never exercised.
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:around line 1213-1216 in main() | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When a malformed baseline file is encountered, the verifier prints a warning and falls back to absolute verification instead of compare_against_baseline().
  WHY: Transient I/O errors or JSON corruption can produce a completely different set of PRE_EXISTING_FINGERPRINT_DRIFT_V1 markers, making verifier output non-deterministic.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:lines 429-461 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The baseline state file is captured before the retry loop begins, but the restore logic does not preserve or restore RESOLVER_FP_BASELINE_STATE_FILE.
  WHY: On retry attempts after a soft failure, the baseline JSON may be missing or stale, defeating the delta-verification contract.
- docs/completed/integration-sync-resolver-self-heal-plan.md:line 626-629 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The link display text says docs/plans/judge-loop-and-reissue-plan.md but the actual relative target resolves to docs/completed/judge-loop-and-reissue-plan.md.
  WHY: Readers following the link from the completed plan are sent to the archived copy instead of the active plan, or get a confusing navigation experience.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:compare_against_baseline(), ~lines 1030-1040 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A fingerprint whose current evaluation returns a check_error is appended to violations immediately, without consulting the baseline to see whether the same error was already present. (2 related items)
  WHY: The current code does not consult baseline_satisfied and blindly appends the violation, causing the verifier to exit 1 for a pre-existing condition the resolver did not touch.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:Stage workflow support files step, lines ~945-984 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: review_conflict_resolve.sh and review_conflict_prepare.sh are listed in both REQUIRED_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS and MAIN_PRIMARY_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPTS.
  WHY: The double install is redundant today and risks confusion about which source is authoritative.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/verify_integration_fingerprints.py:219 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: _read_file_result and _path_exists_result now return (value, error) tuples, but list_violated_files, verify, and compare_against_baseline still allocate caches as dict[str, tuple[...]] and ignore the error component. (2 related items)
  WHY: A persistent read/probe error can be dropped silently, making compare-mode treat a baseline-passing error as satisfied or vice-versa and causing incomplete working-set paths.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:965-984 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Both bootstrap loops unconditionally install the same three scripts, and the required loop can install an older branch copy before the main-primary loop runs.
  WHY: A stale .codex-workflow-src checkout can still bootstrap the old verifier/resolver and never exercise the new baseline/compare logic.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:451 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Baseline capture runs once before the retry loop and the restore logic does not preserve ${RESOLVER_FP_BASELINE_STATE_FILE}.
  WHY: Subsequent retries can compare against stale or re-captured state, defeating the only-fail-on-resolver-introduced-regression contract.
- docs/completed/integration-sync-resolver-self-heal-plan.
